Hi Alessandra —

Thanks for picking up the onboarding for Novaterra. We have a pending PO request and procurement needs a quick checklist from your side to complete vendor setup in Portugal. Two specific asks:

1) Confirm the exact tax identifier you require from Redwood (Portuguese NIF vs EU VAT ID) for supplier setup. Our accounting teams often need clarity whether to record a NIF for the purchasing entity or just the VAT number for cross-border services.

2) Are you requiring e-invoices submitted via the Portal de Faturas e Recibos (or a specific supplier portal)? If so, please share the required invoice fields and any XML/e-invoice schema so we can map our PO/AR system.

I've attached our completed vendor form and a sample PO (Redwood_Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf). If there are any local fiscal rep requirements or if Novaterra needs Redwood to route invoices to a local EU entity (e.g., Redwood Ireland), please let us know so we can surface that to legal/finance.

Proposed next step: if you can confirm the fields and whether reverse-charge applies for services, we can finalize the PO and push the doc for signature.

Thanks —

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the form and the clear asks. Apologies for the delayed reply — collecting the tax details took a beat. Below are the items we need from Redwood and our portal requirements: 

Required supplier metadata for our vendor master (mandatory):
- Company legal name
- Portuguese NIF (if you have a Portuguese fiscal presence) OR EU VAT number (format: PT#########) — if you are a non-resident, we need your EU VAT number and a local contact.
- Company registration country
- Full remittance IBAN and SWIFT/BIC
- Invoices must state the supply description, PO number, invoice number, invoice date, NIF (or VAT ID), VAT rate applied (if any), and tax base.

E-invoicing / portal notes:
- We accept invoices via our supplier portal (https://portal.novaterra.pt/invoices) and via Peppol-compliant XML.
- Required XML fields: supplierNIF, supplierName, invoiceNumber, invoiceDate, poNumber, taxAmount, totalAmount, currency, IBAN.
- If you cannot produce Peppol/structured e-invoice, PDFs uploaded to the portal are accepted but may delay processing.

Tax treatment (high level):
- For software/saas/services supplied by non-EU vendors to a Portuguese VAT-registered buyer, the reverse charge is generally applied and accounted by the buyer (Novaterra). Please include a note on invoices: "Reverse charge — article 196 VAT Directive" where appropriate.
- Where the supplier has a Portuguese establishment (i.e., local branch), Portuguese VAT should be charged.

Docs attached: PT_Tax_Guidance_Novaterra.pdf (guidance for suppliers) and Novaterra_Supplier_Checklist.xlsx.

Action items for Redwood: please confirm which legal entity will receive the PO (Redwood Inference Ltd, Redwood Ireland, or Redwood Inc. US). If you want the PO routed to an EU entity to avoid withholding or additional cross-border form requirements, state the entity and provide the VAT ID/Registration docs.

If helpful we can run a 20-minute alignment call with our AP lead (Maria) on Thursday.

Best,
Alessandra Rossi
Head of Procurement Operations
Novaterra Logistics

Alessandra —

Appreciate the detail, that's super helpful. Quick clarifications from our side before we finalize:

- Redwood does not currently have a Portuguese legal entity. We can route PO and invoices to Redwood Inference Ireland Ltd (EU VAT ID: IE9999999V), which is our EMEA billing entity. Will Novaterra accept invoices from the Ireland entity and apply reverse charge accordingly?

- For Peppol/XML: our billing system can export a minimal e-invoice with the required fields you listed. Laura (cc'd) — can you attach a sample XML export for Novaterra's AP team?

- If Novaterra requires that invoices include the text for reverse-charge, we can add that as a line item. Please confirm exact phrasing you expect on the invoice to avoid rejections.

We can do the quick call on Thursday — suggest 09:30 WEST (10:30 CEST) if that works for Maria. I've attached our vendor form (completed) to this thread for your records.

Thanks —
Ben
